info: Automatically generated model structure log. See accompanying simulation log for more info

LUE.unit: g crop weight per MJ PAR
LUE.reference: Stanghellini (2019), pg. 49. 4.3 is chosen as a middle value, see Fig. 2.13

k.reference: Stanghellini (2019), pg. 49. The value of 0.7 is based on Stanghellini (2019), pg. 39: 'For many greenhouse crops, k has a value between 0.6 and 0.8'

fLeaves.description: Fraction of crop dry mass partitioned to the leaves
fLeaves.reference: Stanghellini (2019), Eq. 2.26. The value of 0.8 is chosen to represent a young vegetative crop

SLA.reference: Stanghellini (2019), Box 2.26. The value of 250 is a middle value for tomato, See Stanghellini (2019), Table 2.1

W.reference: Stanghellini (2019), Eq. 2.25. Note that in Eq. 2.5 (Stanghellini 2019), dW/dt is given in g/m2/day. However, solar light is expressed there as I, in MJ/m2/day. Here we use I instead in W/m2 = J/m2/s (see reference for I). This is multiplied by 1e-6, to convert to MW/m2 = MJ/m2/s. Thus we use I*1e-6 which is in MJ/m2/s, instead of MJ/m2/day. Therefore the unit for dW/dt becomes g/m2/s instead of g/m2/day. The default time unit in GreenLight is s, so W is automatically in g/m2.The initial value of 75 g/m2 is based on Fig. 2.13 (Stanghellini 2019)As a reasonable value for a small crop

I.reference: Stanghellini (2019), pg. 49. Since the default time unit in GreenLight is seconds, It is more convenient to use I in J/m2/s = W/m2 instead of MJ/m2/day. This is adjusted in the definition of W, see there

LAI.reference: Stanghellini (2019), Eq. 2.26. Note that according to the Eq., the LAI growth rate is equal to crop growth rate times fLeaves * SLA / 10000. Therefore LAI is equal to crop dry mass times the same factor

tOut.description: Temperature of the air outside the greenhouse

tSky.description: Apparent temperature of the sky (depends, among other things, on cloudiness)
